label: yes
controls_available: Drag a visible ingredient jar to the mortar to load or replace the active ingredient.
Hold and release the pestle to advance through the 13-notch grind track; in full mode the selected notch is duration-controlled.
Click STIR PATH to advance the active route, with WATER and BELLOWS available for synchronous recovery actions.
Click SEAL to submit the completed preparation.
autonomous_processes: During a full-mode pestle hold, animation-frame callbacks advance grindStep by one notch for each 240 ms of task-clock time, capped by the grind track, and redraw the current notch and path preview.
There is no idle map, route, hazard, or physics update: path traversal and hazard/vortex effects occur synchronously when STIR PATH, WATER, or BELLOWS is clicked.
The CSS pestle-pounding animation runs only while the pestle is held and is not an independent outcome-changing process; the post-failure timeout only hides an overlay.
grouped_control_modes: Full-mode pestle hold/release for duration-based notch selection
Synchronous WATER and BELLOWS recovery movement

clause_i.reason: For histories after a full-mode pestle hold begins, the delayed-optimal release-versus-continue choice depends on the seed-derived route gate's required grind_step, which is not encoded in the action history. The generator makes route-specific grind steps and the grader accepts only the matching ingredient/grind-step gate, so an action-history-only policy cannot be optimal for all such histories.

clause_ii.reason: The visible state includes the filled/current grind notch, the active curved path preview, and the route gate. A 240 ms bounded visual window, including the configured single current frame, supplies the current state and the next grind tick horizon, allowing a visual policy to release at the required notch or continue holding.

clause_iii.reason: Choose a history just before a grind tick when the current notch is the route gate's required notch. If no new input is sent and a delay crosses that tick (with the crossing time still below 240 ms), grindStep advances and the visible path geometry changes; releasing at the formerly aligned notch is then no longer the delayed-optimal action, while success remains possible by reloading/regrinding or using the allowed recovery. The strict loss is route alignment caused by task-state evolution, not a reduced deadline or merely later completion.

common_visible_process: A held full-mode pestle is the common witness: with the pointer held down and no new action, the 240 ms task-clock ticks advance the visible grind notch and recompute the active path preview until release.

pre_run.reason: No autonomous outcome phase follows preparation. Each of the five route commits requires separate visible load/grind/release and synchronous STIR PATH actions, and recovery actions are synchronous as well. The only asynchronous interval is the held pestle, which is itself outcome-affecting; SEAL is administrative. Therefore no generated instance admits the specified no-outcome-action pre-run solution, and no percentage is asserted.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 4 supplies the six-ingredient, five-commit, 13-notch route configuration; full mode uses jar drag and duration-based pestle control, with a 240 ms observation window and one frame.
The exact runtime profile is synchronous with a 240 ms observation window, one frame per observation, and a live 180-second play clock.

The selected control condition supplies the active parameters; route gates and grind steps are generated into the seeded world, while the exported mechanics specify a 240 ms grind tick and fixed path sampling/stride.
The browser visibly renders the route gate, active path preview, and grind track, and advanceGrinding uses task-clock elapsed time to advance one notch per 240 ms while the pestle is held.
STIR PATH, WATER, and BELLOWS resolve movement synchronously, while full-mode input binds jar drag and pestle pointerdown/pointerup to load and duration-controlled grinding.
The pounding animation is conditional on the held-grinding state and the notch track exposes current progress; it does not implement a separate world update.

The grader validates route gates against the ingredient and grind step, replays full-mode hold ticks and releases, applies route/recovery effects at submitted events, and requires all route progress before SEAL passes.
The normal full-mode solver holds the pestle until each target notch and then performs synchronous route/recovery actions, confirming that the duration control is outcome-affecting.
The runtime binds performance time, timers, and animation-frame scheduling to the task clock, so the live-versus-paused schedule controls whether the held-grinding ticks advance.
The environment verifier loads the exported result and delegates authoritative grading to the Apothecary grader rather than using hidden timing shortcuts.
